findings.claim: Dcr=0 region is unit-square minus two quarter-disks of radius √½ centred on t and f; area exactly 1 − π/4

detail.note: Waist claim 'pinched to zero at I' is false: μ=λ diagonal is entirely Dcr=0. Area 1-π/4 is the Euclidean-disk complement; library D uses rotated (Dc,Dct) metric.

findings.claim: φ = 1−|Dct| is the mass that is *decided*, split by μE — a derived quantity, not a modeling choice

detail.note: Multiple equally arithmetic-clean mass assignments induce different partitions.

findings.claim: Cost-derived beats FtC because the model is better, not because the simulator was built to match the ontology

detail.note: Shipped simulator samples (μ,λ) FROM the world labels etau_belief assumes. Hostile generators break that handshake.

findings.claim: Falsifiability of the cost model is real: reality will refute a wrong model via empirical_loss / calibration

detail.note: Module admits calibration≠decision. Quantified: large belief distortion can leave nearly identical decisions. empirical_loss refutes only when ORDERING breaks, not when magnitudes are wrong.

findings.claim: Region count is an OUTPUT not a parameter — nobody chose 4

detail.note: 'Nobody chose 4' is rhetoric. Someone chose four actions and their loss vectors. Count is output OF that choice, exactly as two-region is output of choosing a threshold rule. The gain is that the parameter is now multi-dimensional and checkable — not that parameterisation disappeared.

findings.claim: unreachable() and region_count() are empirical facts about the action set

detail.note: unreachable/region_count are grid estimators, not exact. Coarse grids lie.

findings.claim: Ties cost the average of what they tie between: no free lunch from refusing to choose

detail.note: Average is a scoring convention for set-valued decide, not a physical outcome. Deployment always picks one. Maximin / CVaR would break ties differently. 'No free lunch' holds for risk-neutral expectation of a fair coin between pure actions — a narrower claim.

findings.claim: Cost-curve boundaries capture the interesting non-linear structure of the annotation square

detail.note: Cost boundaries cut Dcr level sets (mean |ΔDcr| > 0). The radial/circular structure of real certainty is not what places the cost-derived walls. Piecewise-linear belief + linear loss => piecewise-linear regions. The notebook's circle is flattened.

findings.claim: The default etau_belief is the natural belief model from the lattice quantities

detail.note: A dumb histogram of the DGP crushes etau_belief on Brier. The lattice readout is not information-theoretically privileged; it's a fixed linear feature map. 'Natural from the logic' ≠ 'good probabilistic model'.

findings.claim: FAULT_CONFLICT / FAULT_SILENCE are instrument failures; the world is 2-valued

detail.note: API names FAULT_* and the worked example assume Reading A (instrument failure). Nothing in Policy enforces it. If the world is Belnap-4-valued, recalibrate/approach are category errors and the worked example's moral doesn't transfer. The module is reading-agnostic in code, reading-A in prose.

findings.claim: etau_belief avoids the silent tie-breaks of labels.py (dc>=0, dct>=0)

detail.note: etau_belief itself is clean on the axes. Any belief that routes through dcr/muER re-imports labels.py's silent dc>=0. The type discipline on Policy.optimal does not protect the belief function.

findings.claim: Core engineering claims: ties returned, dominated actions drop, partition affine-invariant, belief is a distribution
Three Dcr regions are forced by definition; twelve needs FtC; cost-derived is optional refinement

detail.note: Forced-three is real and FtC-free. The twelve-region readout scatters Dcr=0 across multiple labels (measured). Cost-derived is a further optional layer; it does not replace the forced three, and the forced three do not need costs.
